agyos_skill.intent: Provision remote Google Colab GPU/TPU/CPU runtimes and execute Python scripts, notebooks, or shell workloads headlessly via the official Google Colab CLI (`colab`).
agyos_skill.instructions: This runbook guides running notebooks and heavy computational workloads remotely on Google Colab hardware accelerators (T4, L4, A100, H100 GPUs, v5e1/v6e1 TPUs) using the official Google Colab CLI (`google-colab-cli`). The official Google Colab CLI connects your local terminal and agent workflows directly to Colab cloud virtual machines without needing an open browser tab: - **Session Lifecycle**: `colab new` provisions a cloud VM; `colab stop` releases it. - **Kernel Persistence**: State (imports, defined variables, functions) persists across separate `colab exec` calls within the same session. - **Default Directory**: Working directory defaults to `/content`. - **Ephemeral Jobs**: `colab run` provisions a fresh accelerator VM, executes a local script, captures output, and tears down the VM automatically. The CLI supports two authentication modes: ```bash colab --auth=oauth2 sessions ``` Prompts for Google account consent in your default browser on first invocation and caches credentials locally at `~/.config/colab-cli/token.json`. For headless environments using `gcloud`: ```bash gcloud auth application-default login \ --scopes=openid,\ https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform,\ https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email,\ https://www.googleapis.com/auth/colaboratory ``` Verify authentication with: ```bash colab sessions ``` ```bash colab new -s my-session
